title: Syrah or Shiraz
subtitle: Two names, two styles
objectives: Explain where the name Shiraz came from

steps.title: The names
steps.body: Syrah and Shiraz are the same grape. Shiraz is the name used in Australia and South Africa, possibly from an old local spelling. A popular legend links it to the Persian city of Shiraz, but DNA proves the grape is French. James Busby brought cuttings to Australia in 1832.

steps.title: Names as style signals
steps.body: Today, many producers choose the name to signal style. Syrah suggests a cooler, Rhône-like wine: peppery, savoury, medium-bodied. Shiraz suggests a riper, fuller, fruit-forward wine. Some cool-climate Australian producers now label their wines Syrah for this reason.

steps.prompt: James Busby brought Syrah cuttings to Australia in ____.
steps.explanation: Busby's collection in 1832 included Syrah, which became Australia's Shiraz.

steps.title: Cool-climate Shiraz
steps.body: Australia isn't only warm. The Yarra Valley, Canberra District, Great Southern and Adelaide Hills make lighter, peppery Shiraz. Canberra is known for Shiraz co-fermented with Viognier, inspired by Côte-Rôtie. These wines show that Australia's Shiraz can be elegant as well as powerful.

steps.prompt: An Australian wine is labelled Syrah instead of Shiraz. What does this most likely signal?
steps.explanation: Many producers use Syrah to signal a cooler, Rhône-like style.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Syrah and Shiraz are the same French grape
The name often signals style: peppery Syrah, ripe Shiraz
Australia's cooler regions make elegant, peppery Shiraz
